items.abstract: Southeast Asia plays a unique role in the history of research into Early Human societies. Since the end of the 19th century, paleoanthropological discoveries made in Java as well as in China, combined with the discovery of lithic assemblages on cobbles, often on surface within alluvial systems, have highlighted the importance of this region for understanding human dispersal in the Early Palaeolithic in tropical environments. However, the long-term persistence of the ‘pebble/cobble phenomenon’ in Mainland and Island Southeast Asia has contributed to its “marginalisation” in the major narratives of the technical and cognitive evolution of Early Palaeolithic. This peripheral position is largely the result of the historiographical construction of a ‘Far East’ based on Western European and African paradigms. Southeast Asian lithic assemblages have frequently been described as ‘archaic,’ ‘simple,’ or ‘stable,’ a typological reading crystallised by the “Movius line model”. Despite the challenges raised by the identification of bifacial (handaxes) tools and “LCT” assemblages, this framework continues to guide interpretations, sometimes reinforced by the retrospect application of techno-cultural categories such as “Oldowan”, “Acheulean” or “Mode 1/Mode 2” technical systems under the shadow of linear evolutive interpretations about Palaeolithic cultures. Based on recent research conducted in Mainland and insular Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Thailand and the Philippines), this paper offers a critical and methodological review of Middle Pleistocene lithic assemblages in a tropical context. It examines the epistemological impact of inherited conceptual lithic frameworks in the construction of cultural chronologies and typologies, and then develops a techno-structural approach focused on the cobble as a “production matrix”, revealing a diversity of technical solutions integrating heavy and small tools.
items.summary: 《超越继承的石器框架：东南亚中更新世技术行为的新思考》：该文基于柬埔寨、泰国和菲律宾的近期研究，对热带背景下中更新世石器组合展开批判性与方法论回顾，审视“莫维斯线模型”及“奥杜威”“阿舍利”等继承性概念框架对文化年代学与类型学构建的认识论影响，并提出以砾石为“生产母体”的技术—结构研究路径，揭示重型与小型工具并存的技术方案多样性，值得关注东南亚早期人类技术…
items.title: Beyond inherited lithic frameworks: New considerations on Middle Pleistocene technical behaviour in Southeast Asia

items.abstract: Introduction. The study seeks to identify the techno-morphological characteristics of newly discovered core-and-flake industries in the Outer Carpathians and to clarify their adaptive mechanisms in response to the properties of local raw materials. Its primary objective is to define the distinctive features of these local technological strategies and to establish their position within the broader framework of the European Lower Palaeolithic. Methods. The research methodology combines: 1) technological analysis of the archaeological assemblages, and 2) experimental modelling conducted within a qualitative framework. Additionally, Structure-from-Motion (SfM) photogrammetry was used to create detailed 3D models of artefacts to perform diacritical analyses aimed at reconstructing the operational sequences. Particular attention is given to the relationship between raw material, reduction strategy, and flake morphology, as these parameters directly reflect the behavioural and technological choices of early hominins inhabiting the region. Results. The study revealed a specific strategy for processing local raw materials, based on the bipolar on anvil technique and the parallel fragmentation of stone blocks into elongated flakes with straight profiles, referred to as ‘citrons’ and ‘bars’. This method, termed ‘bipolar slicing’, played a key role in the Lower Palaeolithic industries of the Outer Carpathians. Conclusions. The Solne 1 and Solne 2 assemblages represent a local variant of the Lower Palaeolithic technological tradition of the Eastern Carpathians, characterised by the application of bipolar slicing to local sandstone. Together with the Skhidnytsia locality, they form a coherent technological cluster that demonstrates regional specificity in raw material exploitation and reduction principles. These industries are closely related to several other Lower Palaeolithic sites in Ukraine, such as Medzhybizh, Holovchyntsi, and Velykyi Sholes, and are classified as core-and-flake industries.
items.summary: 《双极切片法：外喀尔巴阡下旧石器时代的机遇性技术》：论文考察外喀尔巴阡新发现石核石片工业的技术形态特征，结合技术分析与实验建模及三维摄影测量，揭示以双极砧上技术和石块平行碎裂获取细长石片为特点的“双极切片”策略，并探讨原料、剥片策略与石片形态的关系，值得关注早期人类对本地原料的适应机制。
items.title: Bipolar Slicing the Stone: Opportunistic Technologies in the Lower Palaeolithic of the Outer Carpathians

items.abstract: Cyclostratigraphy and high-frequency sea-level changes of the Cenomanian–Turonian boundary interval (Late Cretaceous) of Central Europe: a reassessment Wilmsen, Markus; Niebuhr, Birgit Newsletters on Stratigraphy, (2026), p. - Abstract The Cenomanian–Turonian boundary interval (CTBI) reflects a tipping point in Earth’s eventful history accompanied by major palaeoenvironmental perturbations, culminating during oceanic anoxic event (OAE) 2. Despite significant geoscientific advances over recent decades in the complex task of deciphering this critical interval in the Cretaceous Earth system, open questions remained about contemporaneous high-frequency sea-level changes, precise stratigraphic correlations and the overall duration of the event. Based on high-resolution integrated stratigraphic calibration and careful sedimentological studies of numerous upper Cenomanian to lower Turonian sections in several sedimentary basins around the Mid-European Island, we report a conspicuous sedimentary cyclicity reflecting high-frequency sea-level changes paced by the long- (E1, 405 kyr) and short-eccentricity (E2–3, ~100 kyr) of the Milankovitch band, superimposed by the precession signal (P1–2, ~20 kyr). Following a major eustatic mid-late Cenomanian 3rd-order sea-level fall (~94.4 Ma), forming sequence boundary SB Ce 5, OAE 2 occurred during an overall transgressive regime within E1 cycles 233 and 232, corresponding to 4th-order high-frequency sequences, separated by a moderate sea-level fall in the latest Cenomanian (~94 Ma). A major transgressive pulse in the early phase of E1 cycle 232 culminated in a global maximum flooding interval across the Cenomanian–Turonian boundary (CTB). Superimposed E2–3 cycles paced high-frequency 5th-order sea-level oscillations, the signatures of which can be correlated across all studied basins. We used time-series analysis of the most complete record (Wunstorf section, Lower Saxony Basin, Germany) to tune the cyclicity to orbital frequencies and anchored our floating time scale to a CTB age of 93.95 Ma. Detailed cyclo- and chemostratigraphic correlations to the Anglo-Paris Basin revealed significant stratigraphic gaps in the Eastbourne section, hitherto considered the European reference section of OAE 2. Furthermore, selected German carbon isotope records across OAE 2 were re-interpreted, and the B, C and D peaks as well as the Holywell Event are now placed higher in these curves. Our new orbital timescale indicates a duration of the positive carbon isotope excursion of OAE 2 (first build-up to the end of the plateau phase) of ~550 kyr and ~700 kyr if the recovery phase is added. The new age model is in good agreement to many other records and resolves previous contradictions regarding shorter durations of OAE 2 in Wunstorf and Eastbourne.
items.summary: 《中欧森诺曼阶—土伦阶界线区间（晚白垩世）的旋回地层学与高频海平面变化：重新评估》：该研究基于高分辨率综合地层校准与沉积学研究，报道了受米兰科维奇长、短偏心率及岁差信号驱动的沉积旋回，重建了高频海平面变化，并将浮游时间标尺锚定于93.95 Ma，进而估算OAE 2碳同位素正漂移持续时间约550至700千年，值得阅读。

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Nitrogen stable isotope (δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N) values are widely used to study dietary behaviors, and recent work also claims to identify periods of stress retrospectively from modest δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N value variation. However, several interrelated variables are believed to impact δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N values including nursing, physiological stress, growth, and nonmilk dietary changes, complicating assessments from archeological individuals.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We investigate associations between δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N patterns and nursing, illness, and growth trajectories in 13 captive rhesus macaques (
                      <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">
                        <jats:italic>Macaca mulatta</jats:italic>
                      </jats:styled-content>
                      ) that consumed largely uniform commercial diets. Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) analysis was applied to measure dentin δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N values sequentially on a sub‐weekly to monthly basis in eight first molars (M1s) and six second molars (M2s).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      By relating dentin spot positions to enamel formation ages, nursing cessation was identified in eight individuals' M1s. Following this consequential dietary transition, pronounced episodic rises in δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N values (+1‰–+3‰) were found in association with severe illness and weight loss in most individuals. These macaques were primarily treated for idiopathic diarrhea, dehydration, and thin body condition, and all study subjects tested positive for
                      <jats:italic>Campylobacter</jats:italic>
                      spp. at least once.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      By integrating high‐resolution δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N value sampling and microscopic tooth growth with colony management records, we demonstrate the potential for δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N value variation in teeth to serve as a proxy for severe illness. Our results highlight the interpretive complexity of δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N value records and underscore the need to account for physiological stressors to avoid over‐simplifying dietary reconstructions, ultimately strengthening insights into health and survivorship of ancient human populations.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Enamel thickness has been extensively investigated in extant and fossil hominids, yet comparable data for hylobatids remain scarce. Existing studies are limited to
                    <jats:italic>Symphalangus syndactylus</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Hylobates lar</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>Hylobates muelleri</jats:italic>
                    and are based on relatively small samples. These studies have characterized enamel thickness as thin in
                    <jats:italic>Symphalangus</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Hy. lar</jats:italic>
                    and intermediate‐thin in
                    <jats:italic>Hy. muelleri</jats:italic>
                    . The polarity of these conditions within Hylobatidae also remains unresolved because stem representatives of the clade have only recently been discovered. Here, we used microcomputed tomography to examine lower third molar (M
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    ) enamel thickness in the stem hylobatid
                    <jats:italic>Kapi ramnagarensis</jats:italic>
                    from the Miocene Lower Siwaliks locality of Ramnagar. We also provide new comparative data from 19 M
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    s of extant hylobatids representing all four living genera. Average (AET) and relative (RET) enamel thickness were quantified from two‐dimensional virtual sections passing through the dentin horns of the two mesial cusps. The M
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    of the single
                    <jats:italic>Kapi</jats:italic>
                    specimen exhibits enamel thickness values within the range observed in extant hylobatids, albeit near the lower end of that distribution, with RET most closely matching that of
                    <jats:italic>Hoolock leuconedys</jats:italic>
                    . Parsimony‐based ancestral state reconstructions of M
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    RET using gap‐weighted coding hypothesize an intermediate‐thin enamel condition at the base of Hominoidea. Within Hylobatidae, the ancestral state was likewise reconstructed as intermediate‐thin enamel. Although RET provides valuable phylogenetic information, its interpretation remains challenging due to the limited data for early catarrhines and hominoids and the pervasive influence of homoplasy. Larger samples will help clarify patterns of enamel thickness variation within hylobatids and across Hominoidea.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene–Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the “white continent” had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mammals. Several discoveries of fragmentary Eocene fossils suggest that Antarctica acted as a land bridge connecting South America to Australia, most notably marsupials. However, fossil mammals are scarce and restricted to a single location—Seymour Island. Here we present two well‐preserved fossil tracks which are the second Antarctic fossil mammal outside Seymour Island and the oldest fossil tracks assigned to an opossum‐like animal in the Cenozoic. They were found in the Fossil Hill Formation on King George Island (lower‐middle Eocene) and exhibit possible opposable thumbs, suggesting an arboreal behavior observable in microbiotheriid and some extant didelphid marsupials living in South America today. They further coincide in time with the rise of scansorial lifestyle in several mammalian lineages. This ichnologic record offers a more comprehensive look into the dispersion and ecology of mammals through the Early Cenozoic of Antarctica, evidencing that small arboreal marsupials inhabited the South Shetland Islands during the Eocene. In addition, the new finding indicates that Antarctica was not merely a corridor, but a rich habitat of dense and productive forest canopies during the middle Eocene.</jats:p>
